narrativeReportMd:
# MedicinalProductPackaged R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes found. R4 `MedicinalProductPackaged` is absent in R6 and the likely successor, `PackagedProductDefinition`, has a redesigned local content model.

## Scope
Compared local R4 resource elements to local R6 successor elements; excluded inherited base-artifact changes.

## Main migration themes
Resource identity replacement, package tree normalization, reference target renames, authorization externalization, batch identifier loss risk, and R6-only modifier/status semantics.

## Highest-impact findings
The root resource replacement, `packageItem`→`packaging` reshape, `Quantity`→`integer` package quantity, merged contained-item model, removed `marketingAuthorization`, and removed `batchIdentifier` are the main migration blockers.

## Follow-up analysis
Review companion resource conversions for `MedicinalProductDefinition`, `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, and `RegulatedAuthorization`, plus any official narrative/conversion guidance if available.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductPackaged` is not present as an R6 resource; migration to `PackagedProductDefinition` is a hard instance-breaking conversion. Top concerns are resource identity, package tree reshape, removed authorization/batch fields, contained-item remodeling, and R6-to-R4 representability gaps.
summary.migrationThemesMd: A safe migration must rename the resource, map `subject` to `packageFor`, rebuild `packageItem` as `packaging`, convert package quantities and contained items, externalize marketing authorization, and preserve or review batch identifiers.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition deltas and successor identity, but medium for exact business-intent mappings because no official ConceptMap, narrative page, or terminology expansions were supplied.

findings.title: R4 MedicinalProductPackaged is absent in R6 and replaced by PackagedProductDefinition

newState.summary: No same-name R6 StructureDefinition exists; PackagedProductDefinition is the likely successor.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 defines `PackagedProductDefinition` with similar package/container scope and retained packaging concepts.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The successor match is based on name, BRR/category metadata, description, local element overlap, and IDMP mappings.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Strict R6 parsers and REST routers will reject `resourceType: MedicinalProductPackaged`; R6 instances likewise require an explicit R6-to-R4 resource-type conversion.

justification.inferredGoal: Align package modeling with the R6 medicinal-product definition family.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the MedicinalProductPackaged resource identity in R6 with broadened definitions, or keep it as a deprecated base resource instead of replacing every resourceType.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of aligning and broadening packaged-product modeling is reasonable, but changing the base resource identity invalidates every R4 instance, profile URL, endpoint, generated class, and FHIRPath rooted at `MedicinalProductPackaged`. The evidence does not show that the R6 goal required a new wire-level resource type rather than carrying the old identity forward with clearer semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `MedicinalProductPackaged` as the R6 resource and updated its definition to cover the broader medically related package scope, adding the R6 content model there. If `PackagedProductDefinition` was also introduced, the old resource could be deprecated for transition, but that would create duplicate resource identities for the same concept. Retaining the old name has a real naming-consistency cost, but it would preserve most existing R4 instances at the root level.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The legacy name would be less consistent with the R6 Definition family and broader packaged-item scope; defining both resource types would duplicate the same domain.

evidence.detail: R6 index contains PackagedProductDefinition and no current MedicinalProductPackaged StructureDefinition.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments show the wire-level resource identity break.

findings.narrativeMd: The resource identity changed. This is the highest-impact local break because every instance, profile, generated class, FHIRPath root, REST type URL, and search name anchored to `MedicinalProductPackaged` must change.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid `MedicinalProductPackaged` JSON is not R6-valid. R6 `PackagedProductDefinition` JSON is not R4-valid. This is a hard validation and runtime dispatch break, not just a semantic difference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert resource type and canonical references first, then apply element-level transforms. Update generated models, endpoints, profile URLs, search names, and fixtures.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 does not carry forward the `MedicinalProductPackaged` resource identity; the plausible successor is `PackagedProductDefinition`. That is a real root-level break for parsers, REST type routes, generated classes, profile URLs, and FHIRPath roots. On a fresh review, the break looks proportionate because the R4 resource was FMM 0 trial-use and R6 broadened the concept from a medicinal-product package to a more general packaged medically related item in the Definition resource family. I found regulatory relevance for IDMP packaging, but not quick evidence that the exact R4 resource identity was broadly deployed enough to overcome the low-FMM stability expectation.
keyEvidence: R6 package index and filesystem: `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductPackaged.json` is absent; `StructureDefinition-PackagedProductDefinition.json` is present.
R4 StructureDefinition: id/type/url are `MedicinalProductPackaged`; R6 successor: id/type/url are `PackagedProductDefinition`.
R4 maturity map and StructureDefinition extensions: MedicinalProductPackaged is trial-use, FMM 0, BRR.
HL7 Global Core IDMP IG continuous build checked: IDMP work covers packaging layers and supply-chain integrity (https://build.fhir.org/ig/scc88/idmp-ig/).
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0/trial-use substantially softens the stability claim for the old resource identity. The IDMP domain is important, but I did not find quick evidence that the R4 wire-level resource name itself has broad production reliance.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: changing `resourceType` and canonical URL means old instances are new-invalid and servers/SDKs/profiles rooted at the old resource need explicit conversion.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could have retained `MedicinalProductPackaged` as the R6 resource name or as a deprecated transition resource, but that would preserve a medicinal-only legacy name for a broader packaged-product model and risks duplicate resource identities for the same concept. This is a plausible alternative, not a clearly low-cost one.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact mechanism, but disagree that the less-breaking alternative is simply `Yes`; the FMM 0 status and duplicate-identity tradeoff make the R6 break probably acceptable.

findings.title: `subject` became `packageFor` and now targets MedicinalProductDefinition

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The old element name is invalid in R6, and reference target validation requires referenced products to be migrated to MedicinalProductDefinition.

justification.inferredGoal: Rename the relationship and align it with the renamed product-definition resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the `subject` element name and clarify it as the product this package is for, with updated or broadened target guidance instead of a same-purpose rename to `packageFor`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The relationship itself survived with the same cardinality and essentially the same meaning. Renaming `subject` to the clearer `packageFor` and following the MedicinalProduct-to-MedicinalProductDefinition transition improves readability, but it is not clearly necessary to accomplish the R6 modeling goal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `subject` as the normative element, updated its definition to match the R6 wording, and adjusted target-profile guidance as part of the broader product-definition transition. If `packageFor` were added as a new synonym, the model would need precedence and consistency rules, so the cleaner alternative is simply living with the older but serviceable name.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The old `subject` name is less explicit, and target-resource migration still depends on the companion product resource transition; allowing both `subject` and `packageFor` would duplicate the same relationship.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example is included; impact is derived from StructureDefinition element definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: The package-to-product link survives but under a new path and target resource family. Code that joins packages to products through `subject` must be rewritten.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old `subject` content is invalid on the R6 successor. Reverse conversion requires changing `packageFor` back to `subject` and converting referenced resources back to `MedicinalProduct`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `subject[]` to `packageFor[]` and rewrite reference resource types only when the referenced resources have also been migrated.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `subject` survives in meaning but not in wire shape: R4 used `MedicinalProductPackaged.subject` as a repeatable reference to `MedicinalProduct`, while R6 uses `PackagedProductDefinition.packageFor` pointing to `MedicinalProductDefinition`. Old instances and client code need a path rename and companion product-resource conversion. The change is breaking, but it tracks the broader product-definition rename and gives the relationship a more explicit name, so for FMM 0 content it does not look disproportionate.

R6 StructureDefinition element `PackagedProductDefinition.packageFor`: 0..*, Reference(MedicinalProductDefinition), definition says it is the product this package model relates to.
R4 maturity map and StructureDefinition extensions: MedicinalProductPackaged is trial-use, FMM 0.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The old path is from FMM 0 trial-use content, so a same-meaning rename does not carry the same stability burden as it would on mature or normative content. Regulatory domain relevance keeps it a real migration concern rather than `No problem`.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the old `subject` element name and `MedicinalProduct` target are not valid at the R6 successor path without a rename and referenced-resource migration.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept `subject` and retargeted it, but that would retain a generic name for a relationship R6 makes more explicit; allowing both `subject` and `packageFor` would duplicate the same relationship and require consistency rules.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the hard-break assessment, but the existing `Yes` alternative judgment overstates how cheap the old name would be once the product resource family also changed.

findings.title: `legalStatusOfSupply` changed from CodeableConcept to repeatable jurisdiction-scoped backbone

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 CodeableConcept object cannot be copied to the R6 backbone array. R6 can express multiple jurisdiction-specific legal statuses that one R4 CodeableConcept cannot preserve.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent legal supply status per jurisdiction.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the old scalar `legalStatusOfSupply` for an unknown or default jurisdiction and add a separate jurisdiction-scoped repeatable element for multi-jurisdiction statuses.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Representing legal supply status per jurisdiction is a reasonable R6 goal, and the R6 backbone directly models the code/jurisdiction pair. A less-breaking design exists, but it would either be incomplete for multi-jurisdiction content or would introduce duplicate representations whose precedence and synchronization could affect regulatory interpretation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base alternative would retain `legalStatusOfSupply` as the legacy default status and add a new repeatable jurisdiction-scoped element. That would keep R4 instances valid and support the new use case, but implementations would need rules for whether the legacy value is equivalent to an entry with unknown jurisdiction and what happens when both forms are populated.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves common R4 data but creates two same-resource places for legal supply status; the old 0..1 CodeableConcept cannot represent multiple jurisdiction-specific statuses without ambiguity.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example is included; impact is derived from StructureDefinition element definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes legal supply status richer by pairing codes with jurisdictions, but the JSON shape changes from a coded value to repeatable objects.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `legalStatusOfSupply.coding` directly under the resource are R6-invalid. R6 multiple jurisdiction entries are not cleanly R4-representable.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap an R4 value as `legalStatusOfSupply[0].code`; populate jurisdiction only if known. Use extensions or manual review for multiple R6 jurisdictions when mapping back.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The legal supply status changes from one CodeableConcept to a repeatable backbone with separate `code` and `jurisdiction`. That invalidates R4-shaped JSON and can make R6-to-R4 conversion lossy when more than one jurisdiction is present. Still, jurisdiction-specific legal status is a strong regulatory modeling goal, and the old scalar could not represent that cleanly. Given FMM 0 trial-use status, the migration burden appears proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition element `MedicinalProductPackaged.legalStatusOfSupply`: 0..1 CodeableConcept.
R6 StructureDefinition element `PackagedProductDefinition.legalStatusOfSupply`: 0..*, BackboneElement with `code` 0..1 CodeableConcept and `jurisdiction` 0..1 CodeableConcept.

EMA ISO IDMP standards overview checked: ISO IDMP covers medicinal product lifecycle, marketing authorization, packaging, and manufacturing (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/human-regulatory-overview/research-development/data-medicines-iso-idmp-standards-overview).
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the compatibility objection, but legal supply status is regulatory content, so the break remains meaningful and requires migration care.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 CodeableConcept at the old path is not the R6 backbone-array shape; R6 jurisdiction-specific repeats are also lossy back to the old scalar.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative would keep the old scalar as a default or unknown-jurisdiction status and add a new jurisdiction-scoped repeat. That preserves old data, but creates two places for legal status and ambiguous precedence when both are present.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing view that this is a hard shape break with only a partial less-breaking alternative; the fresh judgment is that the break is probably acceptable under the low-FMM context.

findings.title: Direct `marketingAuthorization` reference was removed from the package resource

newState.summary: No direct PackagedProductDefinition element; R6 RegulatedAuthorization.subject can target PackagedProductDefinition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: No same-name local element exists; related R6 authorization resource supports package subjects.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old instances carrying `marketingAuthorization` are invalid in R6, and R6-to-R4 conversion must discover related RegulatedAuthorization resources or lose the link.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize authorizations as separate regulated authorization resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated direct `marketingAuthorization` link, possibly retargeted to RegulatedAuthorization, while also supporting the external `RegulatedAuthorization.subject` relationship.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing authorizations into `RegulatedAuthorization` is a reasonable modeling goal, especially because the R6 subject can cover many regulated artifacts. Keeping a local package field would reduce migration breakage but would undermine normalization unless it were only a deprecated mirror with strict consistency expectations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `marketingAuthorization` on the package resource as an optional deprecated reference, either to the R6 authorization resource or as a compatibility bridge. This would preserve R4-shaped packages, but it would leave two authoritative paths for the same relationship and make bundle/server consistency checks necessary.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The direct and inverse authorization relationships could conflict; external authorization resources can carry broader subjects and metadata that a local shortcut cannot fully represent.

evidence.detail: R6 successor has no marketingAuthorization element.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example is included; impact is derived from StructureDefinition element definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: The authorization link changed from a local package field to an external relationship. This is a repository-level migration issue, not a simple rename.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 local authorization references are R6-invalid. R6 packages may not carry enough local information to reconstruct R4 `marketingAuthorization` without querying related resources.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert `MedicinalProductAuthorization` to `RegulatedAuthorization` and ensure it references the migrated package in `subject`. Test bundle and non-bundle migrations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 stored a direct `marketingAuthorization` reference on the package; R6 appears to externalize that relationship through `RegulatedAuthorization.subject`, which can point at `PackagedProductDefinition`. This is more than a local rename because preserving the link may require bundle- or repository-level lookup. The break is real and regulatory-relevant, but a separate authorization resource is a reasonable normalized R6 design, and retaining a local shortcut would create competing authoritative relationship paths.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition element `MedicinalProductPackaged.marketingAuthorization`: 0..1 Reference(MedicinalProductAuthorization).
R6 `PackagedProductDefinition` StructureDefinition checked: no local `marketingAuthorization` element found.
R6 `RegulatedAuthorization.subject`: 0..*, includes Reference(PackagedProductDefinition).
EMA ISO IDMP standards overview checked: regulated medicinal product information includes marketing authorization.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0 lowers the bar for redesign. Marketing authorization is important regulatory data, so the change is still a substantive migration issue, but the maturity context supports accepting a normalized model.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the old local field is not valid on PackagedProductDefinition, and preserving the relationship requires creating or finding a related RegulatedAuthorization.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative would keep a deprecated local `marketingAuthorization` reference, perhaps retargeted to `RegulatedAuthorization`. That would ease R4 instance migration but duplicates the external relationship and raises consistency problems when local and inverse links disagree.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact and partial-alternative assessment, while weighting the low-FMM redesign latitude more heavily in the final judgment.

findings.title: `batchIdentifier` has no local PackagedProductDefinition successor

oldState.summary: 0..* BackboneElement with required `outerPackaging` Identifier and optional `immediatePackaging` Identifier.

newState.summary: No local batchIdentifier, outerPackaging, or immediatePackaging element was found on PackagedProductDefinition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 batch numbering cannot be represented by a same-purpose local R6 field. Mapping it to a generic identifier may change semantics and dropping it can affect traceability.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly separate batch-instance data from package-definition data.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `batchIdentifier` as a deprecated local element, or provide an explicit R6 batch/lot relationship before removing the local structure.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating batch-instance data from package-definition data may be a sound goal, but the available StructureDefinition evidence shows no local R6 successor for the outer/immediate packaging identifiers. Because these identifiers can be important for traceability, removing them without an evident base replacement is not clearly justified on the supplied evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained the repeatable `batchIdentifier` backbone as deprecated while R6 introduced or documented the proper batch/lot artifact and relationship. That alternative is only partial because it preserves a concept that may not belong on a definition resource and could perpetuate mixed definition-versus-instance semantics.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining it preserves traceability but continues carrying batch-instance identifiers on a package definition and may conflict with a cleaner separate batch/lot model; no same-purpose R6 base field was found.

evidence.detail: R4 requires outerPackaging within each batch entry.
No R6 local batchIdentifier successor was found.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example is included; impact is derived from StructureDefinition element definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: Batch numbers are materially important for traceability, but the successor package definition has no obvious local home for them.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `batchIdentifier` content is invalid on R6. R6 cannot round-trip this local structure because no corresponding local element exists.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory use of batch identifiers before migration. Preserve through an agreed extension, related lot/batch artifact, or typed identifier only if local policy makes the semantics explicit.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 had a repeatable `batchIdentifier` backbone with a required outer-packaging identifier and optional immediate-packaging identifier. I could not find a same-purpose local successor on `PackagedProductDefinition`; generic package identifiers and the informative `Product.instance.lotNumber` pattern do not preserve the same outer/immediate package batch distinction on the packaged-product resource. Even though batch data may belong more naturally to product instances than definitions, removing the field without an evident concrete successor is risky for traceability in a regulated packaging domain.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition elements: `batchIdentifier` 0..*, `outerPackaging` 1..1 Identifier, `immediatePackaging` 0..1 Identifier.
R6 `PackagedProductDefinition` StructureDefinition checked: no local `batchIdentifier`, `outerPackaging`, or `immediatePackaging` element found.

R6 product-related StructureDefinitions searched for batch/lot: only `NutritionProduct.instance.lotNumber` and informative `Product.instance.lotNumber` appeared, not a PackagedProductDefinition successor.
HL7 Global Core IDMP IG continuous build checked: packaging layers and supply-chain traceability are in scope; EMA PMS guidance references package submissions for critical medicines.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use normally softens breaks, but batch/package identifiers are traceability- and regulatory-relevant. The low maturity does not fully offset the lack of an obvious successor for this specific data.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 batchIdentifier content is invalid in the R6 successor, and the stronger concern is R6-to-R4/data-loss risk because there is no direct local field to receive or round-trip the identifiers.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could retain `batchIdentifier` as deprecated until a concrete batch/lot resource or relationship is available, or add an explicit package-batch relationship. The tradeoff is real: it may perpetuate instance-level data on a definition resource. But a transitional or explicit successor seems worth standards review because silent remapping to generic identifiers weakens semantics.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact and partial-alternative assessment; the fresh review elevates this to `Revisit` because the local evidence still lacks a concrete traceability-preserving successor.

findings.title: Required repeating `packageItem` became optional single `packaging` tree

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The old `packageItem` array is invalid in R6. Multiple R4 top-level package items cannot be copied into the single R6 top-level packaging field without hierarchy rules or splitting.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize package contents into one packaging tree.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the recursive `packageItem` backbone, or accept both `packageItem` and `packaging` during transition while recommending a single primary packaging tree.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing the package into one packaging tree is a reasonable R6 goal, and the R6 definition explicitly distinguishes packaging containers/components from contained medically related items. The less-breaking alternatives preserve old instances but materially weaken the single-root model and require policy for multiple top-level R4 package items.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative would keep `packageItem` as the recursive base element and clarify that one item is the primary root, or add `packaging` while retaining `packageItem` as deprecated. Either approach would avoid immediate invalidation of R4 data, but it would create duplicate tree shapes or leave the R4 multi-root pattern in the base model indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserving 1..* top-level package items undermines the single-root packaging model and leaves ambiguous handling for multiple roots; accepting both paths duplicates recursive structures.

evidence.detail: R6 nested packaging recurses via contentReference.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example is included; impact is derived from StructureDefinition element definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: The central packaging backbone was renamed and reshaped. This affects serializers, FHIRPath, generated accessors, recursive traversal, and validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data with `packageItem` is R6-invalid. R6 can omit packaging, which cannot satisfy the R4 required package item when converting back.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map one primary R4 package item to `packaging`; map nested package items to `packaging.packaging`. Define policy for multiple top-level R4 package items.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The central packaging tree changes from required, repeatable top-level `packageItem` entries to one optional `packaging` root with recursive nested `packaging`. This invalidates R4 data and requires policy for multiple old top-level package items. The R6 single-root tree is nevertheless a coherent packaging model, especially because it distinguishes packaging containers from contained items. With FMM 0 R4 content, preserving the old multi-root shape in base R6 would likely be a worse long-term design.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition element `MedicinalProductPackaged.packageItem`: 1..*, BackboneElement; recursive child `packageItem.packageItem`.
R6 StructureDefinition element `PackagedProductDefinition.packaging`: 0..1, BackboneElement; recursive child `packaging.packaging` uses contentReference.
HL7 Global Core IDMP IG continuous build checked: packaging layers are central to IDMP modeling.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the stability concern for a central content-model redesign. Packaging is regulatory-relevant, so the break is not dismissed, but the maturity level supports accepting a cleaner model.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old `packageItem` arrays are not valid at the R6 path, and multiple old roots require a conversion policy into one packaging tree.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative would retain `packageItem` as deprecated or accept both tree shapes during transition. That would preserve old JSON but duplicate recursive structures and leave ambiguous handling of multiple top-level package roots.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing hard-break and partial-alternative characterization; the final judgment is softened by the low FMM and the plausible R6 modeling benefit.

findings.title: `packageItem.quantity` changed from required Quantity to optional integer

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON shape changes from a Quantity object to an integer primitive. Unit-bearing, decimal, comparator, or missing R4 quantities need policy decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate package-layer counts from contained-item amounts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the packaging quantity as `Quantity` and constrain or recommend whole-number count semantics, while using `containedItem.amount` for item amounts.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R4 definition already described package quantity as the count of packages at the current layer, with the outermost always 1. Replacing a required `Quantity` object with an optional integer is a hard serialization and codegen break that does not appear necessary to separate package-layer counts from contained-item amounts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `packaging.quantity` as `Quantity` with a narrowed definition, best-practice invariant, or profile guidance requiring whole-number count usage for package layers. `containedItem.amount` could still carry item quantities such as tablets or milliliters. The tradeoff is weaker base-level enforcement of integer-only counts, but that is a moderate validation cost rather than a need for a breaking datatype replacement.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping `Quantity` permits broader forms than a pure integer and needs guidance for units, decimals, and comparators, but it preserves old JSON and avoids duplicate same-fact fields.

evidence.detail: R6 uses Quantity for contained item amount.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example is included; impact is derived from StructureDefinition element definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: Package quantity has a direct codegen and serialization break: object-valued `Quantity` becomes primitive integer.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Quantity JSON is invalid for R6 `integer`. R6 omitted quantity cannot satisfy R4 required quantity if reconstructing R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert only whole-number package counts to integer. Preserve or review units/comparators; use `containedItem.amount` for actual item quantity when appropriate.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `packageItem.quantity` changes from a required `Quantity` object to an optional integer on `packaging.quantity`. That is a clear serialization and code-generation break, and R4 unit-bearing, decimal, comparator, or missing values need migration policy. The R6 definition narrows the field to the count of packaging items at a layer and moves actual contained-item amounts to a separate Quantity field, which is a reasonable computability goal. For FMM 0 content, the break appears proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition element `MedicinalProductPackaged.packageItem.quantity`: 1..1 Quantity; definition says the outermost package quantity is always 1.
R6 StructureDefinition element `PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.quantity`: 0..1 integer; definition says it is only the count of packaging items at this layer.
R6 StructureDefinition element `PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.containedItem.amount`: 0..1 Quantity for quantities such as tablets or milliliters.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The required R4 field is from FMM 0/trial-use content, so the datatype break carries less standards-stability weight. Packaging quantities are still business-relevant, which is why this remains a real migration issue rather than `No problem`.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a JSON Quantity object is invalid where R6 expects an integer primitive; non-whole or unit-qualified R4 quantities require review.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping `Quantity` and constraining it to whole-number count semantics would be less breaking, but it would preserve units, comparators, and decimal forms that R6 is trying to exclude from package-layer counts. That alternative is partial, not clearly superior.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the high-impact mechanism, but disagree with the existing `Yes` alternative judgment; the less-breaking Quantity design weakens the R6 integer-count goal.

findings.title: Separate `device` and `manufacturedItem` arrays merged into `containedItem.item` CodeableReference

oldState.summary: Separate 0..* Reference arrays for DeviceDefinition and MedicinalProductManufactured.

newState.summary: Repeatable containedItem backbone with required CodeableReference item and optional amount.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by element meaning, definitions, and nearby content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old direct arrays are invalid in R6; target resources and datatype changed. R6 can contain concepts and additional resource types that R4 cannot represent.

justification.inferredGoal: Unify package contents and support broader medically related item types.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the old `device` and `manufacturedItem` arrays while adding a unified `containedItem` CodeableReference path for new item categories and concept-only entries.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Unifying contained package items and allowing broader medically related targets is a reasonable R6 goal. A compatibility design could preserve common R4 arrays, but it would not give R6 one canonical representation and would require implementations to merge or reconcile old arrays with the new CodeableReference model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial less-breaking base design would retain `device` and `manufacturedItem` as deprecated child arrays and add `containedItem.item` for the broader R6 set. This would preserve R4 instances for devices and manufactured items, but new targets such as packaged products, biologically derived products, nutrition products, and concept-only entries would still need the new path, creating long-term duplicate content channels.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Old arrays cover only two R4 target classes and duplicate the new canonical path; conflicting or redundant representations could persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R6 contained item is CodeableReference with broader targets.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example is included; impact is derived from StructureDefinition element definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 replaces two direct arrays with a unified contained-item model. This is expressive but not wire-compatible.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 fields are invalid in R6. R6 CodeableReference concepts or added targets have no direct R4 equivalent.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create one `containedItem` per old device/manufactured item. Convert `MedicinalProductManufactured` references to `ManufacturedItemDefinition`; handle concept-only or new target types with extensions/manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 represented contained package contents through separate `device` and `manufacturedItem` reference arrays. R6 replaces that with repeatable `containedItem.item` CodeableReference entries that can point to manufactured items, devices, packaged products, biologically derived products, nutrition products, or a concept. This is a real wire and SDK break, and R6-only targets or concept-only entries do not round-trip to R4. The R6 design is more expressive and gives one canonical contained-item pattern, so the break is probably acceptable for FMM 0 trial-use content.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition element `MedicinalProductPackaged.packageItem.device`: 0..* Reference(DeviceDefinition).
R4 StructureDefinition element `MedicinalProductPackaged.packageItem.manufacturedItem`: 0..* Reference(MedicinalProductManufactured).

R6 StructureDefinition element `PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.containedItem.item`: 1..1 CodeableReference with targets ManufacturedItemDefinition, DeviceDefinition, PackagedProductDefinition, BiologicallyDerivedProduct, and NutritionProduct.
R6 `containedItem.amount` is a separate Quantity, supporting the new unified contained-item model.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use lowers the expected compatibility burden for replacing two early package-content arrays. Regulatory and supply-chain relevance keeps the migration material, but does not by itself require preserving the old split arrays.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old direct arrays are not valid in R6; R6 CodeableReference concepts and additional target types are lossy when converting back to R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative would keep deprecated `device` and `manufacturedItem` arrays while adding `containedItem`. That preserves common R4 data but creates duplicate content channels and reconciliation rules, and it still cannot cover R6 concept-only or new-target content through the old paths.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing hard-break and partial-alternative analysis; the final judgment is that the R6 unification is proportionate.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding a lifecycle status that can indicate a record should not be treated as valid is reasonable for an R6 definition resource. This finding is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue in the calibration sense because the new modifier is optional and does not invalidate R4 content by its absence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Not applicable. The compatibility concern is not preserving an R4 field in the R6 base design; it is that R6 processors must not ignore the new modifier and R6-to-R4 conversion cannot represent it locally without an extension or sidecar.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The remaining cost is runtime and R6-to-R4 handling: R6 consumers must process the modifier, and R4 conversion needs an extension or sidecar if status is present.

findings.narrativeMd: This is an additive R6 element but a material runtime risk because modifier elements change safe processing obligations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 instances are not broken by absence of status. R6-to-R4 loses lifecycle validity unless preserved in an extension or sidecar metadata.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated models and business rules to process `status`; do not treat it as ignorable descriptive text.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible transition would have required keeping the old resource/element shape or publishing a normative conversion map. That would lower migration cost but preserve duplicated or ambiguous representations during the transition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds an optional `status` modifier element; R4 had no corresponding local field. This does not make any R4 package content invalid by absence of `status`. R6 processors must respect the modifier when it is present, and R6-to-R4 conversion may need an extension or sidecar to preserve it, but that is an additive R6 processing concern rather than a R4-to-R6 compatibility problem for this path.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition element `PackagedProductDefinition.status`: 0..1 CodeableConcept, isModifier=true, preferred binding to publication-status.
R4 `MedicinalProductPackaged` local element set checked: no local lifecycle status modifier.
Existing report itself marks hardInstanceBreaking as `No` for this finding.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use further reduces concern because no old field is invalidated. The R6 modifier status is important for R6 consumers, but it does not create an old-valid/new-invalid break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 status has no local R4 field, but the change is optional and additive for R4-to-R6 migration.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for preserving R4 instances. A non-modifier status would be easier to ignore but would undermine the stated R6 safety rule that status can indicate the record should not be treated as valid.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing high overall impact as a R4-to-R6 compatibility finding; the existing report correctly noted it is not a hard instance break, but treated the additive modifier as too severe.
